title: A drop cap and a lead paragraph
summary: ::first-letter floated into a big drop cap, and ::first-line in small caps to open an article.
explanation: ::first-letter selects the first letter of a block, with no extra markup. Floating it left lets the next lines wrap around it, and a big font-size with line-height: 1 makes it span about three lines.
::first-line selects whatever ends up on the first line at the current width, so it changes as the column narrows. Here it is uppercase with a little letter-spacing, a classic magazine opening.
Only the first paragraph gets the effect because the selectors use .lead, not p.
tryThis: Change the drop cap's font-size to 72px and adjust its line-height until it lines up with three lines.
Remove float: left: the letter becomes a giant first character on its own line.
Narrow the article to 300px and see how ::first-line follows the new first line.

children.text: Once the layout was done, the team turned to the words. A page that is easy to read keeps its lines short, its spacing generous and its openings inviting, and a drop cap is one of the oldest ways to invite a reader in.
The second paragraph is normal text. Only the lead paragraph gets the drop cap, because the selector names its class.
